chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants, and He is the All-Knowing of what is in the breasts, the Most Wise of the wise, the All-Seeing of the seers, the Nearest of the near, the Foremost of the approaching, the Best of the Reckoners, the Most Merciful of the merciful, the Most Just of the just, the All-Seeing of the seeing, the Most Decisive of the deciders.

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who does injustice

ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and mercy in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the divine attributes of justice (*Adl*), knowledge, and mercy to affirm Allah's fairness, countering the notion of divine tyranny. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine that God’s judgment is inherently just and that He is the ultimate Reckoner, providing theological grounding for human accountability.
